items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Fats Waller would bring his whole band in and jam with us... I said no black musicians came in there. That's not true.

ctx.x: say, during the war, World War II. But up until that time there were many restaurants that you couldn't go into, you know, they wouldn't serve you. Hotels. You couldn't stay -- Chicago was a terribly prejudiced town. But any way, they had some good bands.

At this time, when I was working at the Three Deuces with Roy, all -- as I said, all the musicians came in. That's -- oh, just Red Norville, Mildred Bailey, their band of just all the great bands. So it was kind of a showcase, and we had a very good band, and we were broadcasting from there. Basie had a little six piece band or seven piece band that was broadcasting from Kansas City at the time, and they came on just before, so we would sit in the car and hear them, and then when they'd go off we'd rush in and…
